content.text:
I submitted index 20 (Cr 0.32 / Sb 0.68) as the best composition. It had the highest measured EQE, 0.028%.

I used all 3 merit measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.30 | 0.011 | Cr-rich side; the model predicts a ~2.0 eV band gap for Cr₅Sb₃O₁₆ here |
| 14 | 0.48 | 0.021 | Close to the 1:1 CrSbO₄ composition (predicted gap ~2.0 eV) |
| 20 | 0.68 | 0.028 | Close to CrSb₂O₆, which the stability model puts almost on the convex hull, so it should form readily |

EQE rose steadily as the Sb fraction went up. That suggests the true optimum may lie further toward the Sb-rich end (indices 21–28), but I had no budget left to check. Those compositions are unmeasured, so they earn nothing towards the score.

Two caveats:
- **Band gaps:** the model predicted about 0.75–0.96 eV for the Sb-rich phases. That seems too low for these oxides, so I gave it little weight. The trend in the measured data drove the last choice.
- **XRD:** I never ran it, so which crystal phases are actually present at each composition is inferred from the model, not measured.
